arguments.value: Greyhound referred for bilateral Dioctophyme renale infection with anorexia, hematuria, weight loss, and severe azotemia/uremic syndrome causing non-oliguric stage 5 AKI; ultrasound confirmed bilateral renal parasitism and the dog underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy and bilateral nephroscopy with removal of multiple worms, followed by improvement and discharge with residual CKD stage 3, proteinuria, and prehypertension.
